summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, and G-tube dependence was readmitted three days after discharge due to worsening nausea, vomiting, and dehydration. She presented with acute kidney injury, metabolic alkalosis, and hypokalemia, all of which resolved with IV hydration and electrolyte repletion. During admission, she developed aspiration pneumonitis after vomiting, prompting a course of levofloxacin, and had ongoing suicidal ideation, requiring intermittent 1:1 sitter monitoring and psychiatric evaluation. Imaging showed paralytic ileus without obstruction, and a midline was placed for IV access due to limited central venous options. She improved clinically, was stabilized on oral medications, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up, antibiotic completion, and continued social work support for TPN insurance approval.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food or vomitus
